bugs.what: Navigation between wilderness rooms uses relative compass directions ('one north and two east of X') that don't always match actual movement outcomes 1:1 — occasionally moving a stated direction landed in a room whose own position description didn't line up with the prior room's stated bearings, requiring repeated 'get your bearings' calls to re-orient.

Failed skill checks (especially will checks) escalate the DC on retry ('raised 1 by failed tries') but the escalation combined with already-low will scores could create a losing spiral on companion-dispute diplomacy checks, several of which I failed twice in a row despite ~60% listed odds.

The 'Column' consequence quest (Ironbound burning hollows) triggered from accepting the Regent's Commission/writ, but gave no actionable way to intervene before turns ran out — it just periodically announced more hollows burning as flavor text with no clear stop mechanism presented to the player.

confusions: It was never fully clear whether declining to promise the reeve about the barrow doors vs. getting the priest's blessing first was the 'correct' sequencing — both seemed to work fine in the end, but the game telegraphed real tension there that didn't end up mattering much.

The 'swear the oath yourself' warning at the Wardmoor oath-stone ('whoever swears it stands in it from then on') read as an irreversible/dangerous commitment but turned out to be just a rank-flavor status change; a clearer warning of actual mechanical stakes (or lack thereof) would help players decide without fear of a hidden softlock.

It was unclear how many of the 15 holds needed real attention vs. how much was intentionally leave-able; the status screen's 'a hold seen whole is forty to seventy turns' framing helped but I still wasn't sure if partial exploration of a hold (e.g. just its main hollow, skipping side content) counted fully toward 'settled.'
suggestions: Add a lightweight compass/minimap summary to 'get your bearings' so multi-step wilderness navigation is less trial-and-error.
Show a numeric percentage alongside 'roll N+ on the die' so players can gauge risk without doing mental math, especially for checks with stacking modifiers.

Give clearer in-fiction signposting for time-sensitive world-state consequences (like the Ironbound column) so players know whether/how they can intervene versus just being told about damage after the fact.
Consider flagging truly irreversible/character-altering choices (like binding oaths) more distinctly from ones that are just flavorful rank changes, so players can calibrate risk correctly.
